_note: The claim extractor's grammar, with a reason per rule. A summary is split into sentences (claims); each claim is split into atoms by these rules; each atom is matched against the sources the template merged in. A claim with no atom is unverifiable and is counted, never gated on. Vocabulary rules run before pattern rules, so a product name the export knows wins any overlap.

sentence_split.reason: a sentence ends at a full stop, exclamation or question mark followed by white space and a capital, a dollar sign or a quote; dates and amounts never contain that sequence

money.reason: a dollar figure is the atom a reviewer checks least and a customer notices first; contradicted when the sentence plays the amount role (an offer, a refund, a credit, a repair, a replacement, a charge) and the field holds a different figure

date.reason: ISO dates are how the export writes every date field and how the fixture's comments quote them; an unseen date is unsupported, never contradicted, because a date can belong to many roles

duration.reason: warranty lengths, windows, steps and percentages come from knowledge chunks and comments; a figure with a unit from nowhere is unsupported; `units` is not a unit here because product names end in a digit (Aero 2 units)

identifier.reason: serial, return, order and invoice numbers are the atoms a model invents most fluently; the fixture's exports carry them in comments when they exist

priority.reason: a picklist value with one field counterpart; contradicted when the field says otherwise and no comment says it

status.reason: as priority; matched case-sensitively so `closed the ticket` is prose and `Closed` is a value

product.reason: the product names come from the export's own picklist values and the chunk index; a product the case is not about is a contradiction unless a comment names it

contact.reason: a person's name from another case is the fault a reviewer cannot see without the record open

action.reason: what the agent did or offered; supported only when a comment or a field says it, because the subject line never does

verdict_order_reason: a claim takes the worst verdict of its atoms; contradicted outranks mis-grounded outranks unsupported, and a claim with no atom is unverifiable
